title: Single-Digit Lucas Step: C(a,b) coprime to p ⟺ b ≤ a (for a < p)
content: The atom of the whole argument: within the first p rows of Pascal's triangle there are no nontrivial multiples of p. For a row index a < p, the factorial identity C(a,b)·b!·(a−b)! = a! shows C(a,b) ∣ a!, while a < p forces p ∤ a! (Nat.Prime.dvd_factorial gives p ∣ a! ⟺ p ≤ a). Hence any prime dividing C(a,b) must come from the trivial vanishing C(a,b) = 0, i.e. b > a. The iff form not_dvd_choose_lt_iff then reads: a single base-p digit C(a,b) survives mod p exactly when the column digit b fits under the row digit a. This is the per-digit survival criterion that the Lucas congruence multiplies across all positions.
relatedConcepts: prime not dividing a small factorial

title: Lucas' Divisibility Criterion: p ∣ C(n,k) ⟺ some digit kᵢ > nᵢ
content: The headline original contribution. Pick a base exponent a with n, k < pᵃ so every digit beyond position a vanishes. Mathlib's Lucas congruence Choose.choose_modEq_prod_range_choose_nat gives C(n,k) ≡ ∏_{i<a} C(nᵢ,kᵢ) (mod p), so p ∣ C(n,k) iff p divides the digit product. Nat.Prime.dvd_finset_prod_iff reduces that to p ∣ C(nᵢ,kᵢ) for a single position i, and the single-digit step converts it to nᵢ < kᵢ. The reverse direction handles out-of-range positions i ≥ a by noting both digits are 0 there, so a strict digit inequality forces i < a. This precise WHICH-columns-die statement is not a named Mathlib lemma — only the congruence and the single-digit Nat.dvd_choose are provided upstream.
relatedConcepts: prime divides a product iff a factor
base-p digit extraction n/pⁱ mod p

title: Digit-Dominance Form: survival ⟺ k digit-dominated by n
content: The contrapositive of the divisibility criterion, packaged as the survival statement. De Morgan turns ∃ i, nᵢ < kᵢ into ∀ i, kᵢ ≤ nᵢ (not_exists then pointwise not_lt). The result reads: C(n,k) is NOT divisible by p exactly when every base-p digit of k is at most the corresponding digit of n — k is 'digit-dominated' by n, equivalently the subtraction n − k needs no borrow in base p. This is the clean, reusable form of Lucas' theorem describing precisely which entries of row n survive mod p, and the bridge to both Fine's count and Kummer's valuation.
relatedConcepts: De Morgan duality of the divisibility criterion

title: Kummer's Carry Count: ν_p(C(n,k)) = number of base-p carries
content: kummerCarries p n k counts the positions i ≥ 1 where the base-p addition of k and n − k overflows pⁱ, i.e. pⁱ ≤ (k mod pⁱ) + ((n−k) mod pⁱ). Kummer's theorem (1852) — the deepest of the three classical results — states this carry count IS the p-adic valuation ν_p(C(n,k)). The Lean proof factorization_choose_eq_carries is Mathlib's Nat.factorization_choose instantiated at the upper bound b = n+1, which is admissible since log_p n ≤ n. Where Lucas only sees the binary survives/dies dichotomy, Kummer resolves the full exponent of p, with each carry contributing one factor of p.
prerequisites: Nat.log and the bound log p n ≤ n

title: Zero-Carry Stratum (Valuation Form): survival ⟺ no carries
content: For k ≤ n the binomial C(n,k) is nonzero, so divisibility by p is equivalent to its p-adic valuation being at least 1 (Nat.Prime.dvd_iff_one_le_factorization). Substituting Kummer's carry count for that valuation and closing with omega yields: ¬ p ∣ C(n,k) ⟺ kummerCarries p n k = 0. This is the valuation-level statement of the zero-carry stratum — an entry survives mod p exactly when the base-p addition k + (n−k) is entirely carry-free. It is the half of the keystone biconditional contributed by Kummer; the other half (carry-free ⟺ digit dominance) follows from Lucas' criterion.

title: The Keystone Bridge: no carries ⟺ digit dominance ⟺ survives mod p
content: The central fusion of the entry. Chaining the valuation-form zero-carry statement (Kummer) with the digit-dominance criterion (Lucas) gives a single biconditional valid for k ≤ n: kummerCarries p n k = 0 ⟺ ∀ i, kᵢ ≤ nᵢ ⟺ ¬ p ∣ C(n,k). Read across the three sides this unifies Kummer 1852 (no carries), Lucas 1878 (digit dominance), and Fine 1947 (survival mod p) into one statement — the carry-free, borrow-free, and non-divisible columns are literally the same set. The base-p addition k + (n−k) carries nowhere exactly when the subtraction n − k borrows nowhere, the classic carry/borrow duality made precise.
relatedConcepts: Granville's synthesis of the three theorems

title: Recovering Fine's Count as the Zero-Carry Stratum
content: Closes the loop back to the parent. The parent Fine entry defines fineRow p n = {k ≤ n : ¬ p ∣ C(n,k)} and proves its cardinality is the digit product ∏ᵢ(nᵢ+1), but never says which columns are counted. Here fineRow_eq_digitDominated rewrites that set, column by column via not_dvd_choose_iff_forall_digit_le, as exactly the digit-dominated columns {k ∈ range (n+1) | ∀ i, kᵢ ≤ nᵢ}. So Fine's count is literally the number of carry-free columns — the size of the zero-carry stratum — and the parent's mysterious surviving set acquires an explicit description. The proof is a single Finset.ext plus and_congr_right against the Lucas criterion.

title: Worked Examples at p = 2 (kernel decide, no native_decide)
content: Four concrete instantiations ground the abstract chain, all discharged by kernel `decide` so the file stays axiom-free (no Lean.ofReduceBool from native_decide). 2 ∣ C(4,1) = 4: with 4 = 100₂ and 1 = 001₂, the digit 1 > 0 at position 0 forces divisibility. 2 ∤ C(4,0) = 1: column 0 is always digit-dominated, so it always survives. ν₂(C(6,3)) = 2: with 3 = 11₂, adding 3 + 3 in binary carries at both bits, so the 2-adic valuation is 2 (C(6,3) = 20 = 2²·5). |fineRow 2 5| = 4: row 5 = 101₂ has surviving columns {0,1,4,5}, matching Fine's digit product (1+1)(0+1)(1+1) = 4.
